record.paper_title: Open Problems in the Topology of Manifolds
record.original_question: Using the same cancellation-genus setup for connected compact smooth 2q-manifolds, is there a finitely presented group pi and epsilon in {+1,-1} for which the epsilon-cancellation genus cg_epsilon(pi) is at least 2? Equivalently, can one find 2q-manifolds M and N with fundamental group pi such that M # W_g is diffeomorphic to N # W_g for some g, but M # W_1 and N # W_1 are not diffeomorphic?

evidence.quote: Problem B. (Is the cancellation genus ever greater than one?) Is there a finitely presented group pi and epsilon in {+/-1} such that cg_epsilon(pi) >= 2?
i.e. is there a pair of 2q-manifolds M and N with pi1(M) isomorphic to pi1(N) isomorphic to pi such that we have M#Wg isomorphic to N#Wg for some g but M#W1 and N#W1 are not diffeomorphic?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $q\geq 1$ be an integer and let $W_g := \#_{i=1}^g (S^q\times S^q)$ denote the $g$-fold connected sum of $S^q\times S^q$ with itself (with $W_0 := S^{2q}$). For a finitely presented group $\pi$ and a sign $\varepsilon\in\{+1,-1\}$, consider the class $\mathcal{M}_\varepsilon(\pi)$ of connected closed smooth oriented $2q$-manifolds $M$ with $\pi_1(M)\cong\pi$, taken up to orientation-preserving diffeomorphism if $\varepsilon=+1$ and up to (possibly orientation-reversing) diffeomorphism if $\varepsilon=-1$. Define the $\varepsilon$-cancellation genus $\mathrm{cg}_\varepsilon(\pi)$ to be the smallest integer $g_0\geq 0$ such that for all $M,N\in\mathcal{M}_\varepsilon(\pi)$ with $M\#W_g\cong N\#W_g$ for some $g\geq 0$, one already has $M\#W_{g_0}\cong N\#W_{g_0}$ (in the appropriate diffeomorphism sense determined by $\varepsilon$).

Question: Does there exist a finitely presented group $\pi$ and a sign $\varepsilon\in\{+1,-1\}$ such that $\mathrm{cg}_\varepsilon(\pi)\geq 2$? Equivalently, does there exist (for some $q\geq 1$) a pair of closed smooth $2q$-manifolds $M$ and $N$ with $\pi_1(M)\cong\pi_1(N)\cong\pi$ such that $M\#W_g$ is diffeomorphic to $N\#W_g$ for some $g\geq 1$, while $M\#W_1$ is not diffeomorphic to $N\#W_1$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem ("Problem B") about whether the cancellation genus for stable diffeomorphism of even-dimensional manifolds can ever exceed one. Web search did not reveal any published resolution; literature on connected-sum cancellation problems (Kreck, Crowley–Sixt, Friedl–Nagel–Powell–Teichner, and surveys on connected sum decompositions of high-dimensional manifolds) treats related stable classification questions but does not appear to settle this specific question.

status_evidence.title: Connected Sum Decompositions of High-Dimensional Manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses cancellation phenomena for connected sums in high dimensions, including examples where M#(S^5 x S^{k-5}) ≅ N#(S^5 x S^{k-5}) without M ≅ N.
status_evidence.claim: Related cancellation/stable classification literature does not resolve the cancellation-genus ≥ 2 question.

status_evidence.title: Connected sum decompositions of high-dimensional manifolds (Matrix notes)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of connected sum decompositions and stable diffeomorphism in high dimensions.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the cancellation-genus ≥ 2 problem is reported in this survey.
